react_result.final_narrative_text: Six of the eight differentially abundant metabolites form a biologically coherent tryptophan-centric module. RaMP ORA across four databases (KEGG, Reactome, SMPDB, WikiPathways) identifies tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelming top hit with an FDR of 1.08e-15 and fold-enrichment of 857.8 (KEGG:map00380), rank 2 WP:WP465 (FDR 3.66e-12, fold 622.6), and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 6.49e-09, fold 2105.5) — all significant at the genome-wide threshold. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returns hsa00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the sole pathway at p = 1.79e-07, with five of the eight inputs (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine) overlapping its 41-member KEGG roster. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis on the empirical human_mfn network corroborates the same module at p = 8.40e-05, matching six of the input compounds plus an additional D-tryptophan variant to its 14-member tryptophan metabolism set — the only pathway with double-digit compound coverage. All six driver metabolites are verified members of the RaMP-reported pathway rosters: L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), tryptamine (C00398), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and quinolinic acid (C03722). Molybdenum (C00150) and L-proline (C00148) did not contribute to the tryptophan signal; proline appeared only in a secondary arginine/proline metabolism hit of lower statistical weight. The convergent pattern across ORA and m/z-network paradigms indicates that the treatment specifically perturbs tryptophan catabolism, displacing flux across the serotonin-melatonin branch and the kynurenine/quinolinic acid arm — consistent with immune activation or indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) induction. The IDO pathway (WP:WP5414) is the most focused sub-module, directly linking L-tryptophan depletion to 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid accumulation, implicating the NAD+ biosynthetic trunk as the downstream effector of the shift.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380) as the overwhelmingly dominant affected pathway in this metabolomics dataset. No other pathway appeared in the top 5 of any tool. A secondary consensus emerged around the serotonergic/melatonin biosynthesis submodule (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 1.39e-08) and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 6.49e-09), both of which are biologically nested within tryptophan catabolism. MetaboAnalystR PSEA (the community-standard KEGG-only tool) independently confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00380 pathway at rank 1 with p = 1.79e-07, hitting five of these compounds. Mummichog, which uses m/z-based network activity on the human metabolic function network, placed 'Tryptophan metabolism' at rank 1 with p = 8.4e-05, again with six matched compounds across its empirical compound set. No other pathway appeared in the top 5 of any tool. A secondary consensus emerged around the serotonergic/melatonin biosynthesis submodule (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 1.39e-08) and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 6.49e-09), both of which are biologically nested within tryptophan catabolism. The biological story is a broad perturbation of tryptophan fate: both the neuroactive serotonin-melatonin axis and the immunomodulatory kynurenine/quinolinic acid arm are simultaneously affected in the treatment group, consistent with conditions that alter tryptophan allocation such as inflammation, indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase induction, or microbiota-driven catabolism.
